TASK A: CONCEALMENT AFTER DISCOVERY. Files: tests/test_concealment_repro.py and /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/stage5-notes/concealment-repro.md.
QUESTION (from .plans/implementation_plan.md Stage 5 item 1): 'Reproduce concealment after discovery and a subsequent NPC encounter. If the discovery-hidden state is being reused for concealment, separate possession, observer knowledge and concealment through validated facts. If no confusion is reproduced, close the item with evidence.'
KNOWN SO FAR (verify, do not trust): 'discovery-hidden' is worldkeeper's wk_hidden fact: seeded from items with hidden: true (the memory card in data/stories/continuity-initiative/world.yaml) and removed one-way by World.reveal() (packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model.py ~lines 854-860, 352, 485, 664); worldkeeper refuses to move a hidden thing; storygame/runtime/item_facts.py ~line 1552 refuses narrated item_facts for a hidden thing. grep found no concealment state in storygame/. The card starts under the drawer in scene 1A (plot.md item placement) and 1B/1C scenes reuse it.
INVESTIGATE AND PIN: (1) Discovery: drive the real engine (scripted provider) through the 1A discovery of the memory card and show the exact facts before and after (wk_hidden gone, who or what is the card's parent/place, visibility, and the story facts such as memory_card_recovered). (2) Possession: show what a narrated item_facts update 'Kristin pockets/takes the memory card' does (place becomes Kristin) and what a narrated 'Kristin hides the card under the seat / in the glovebox' does (accepted as a place move, refused, or ignored; name the exact validation path and issue string). (3) Re-hiding: show that no narrated or authored operation can set wk_hidden again (search the repo for every writer of wk_hidden and for any 'concealed', 'hidden' or 'pocket' state axis); state it plainly. (4) Observer knowledge: for the first scene where an NPC meets the player after the card is found (1B, the man watching Kristin, or Brandon), render the narrator request (the dict CloudflareTurnProvider builds with context['knowledge_context'] and the THINGS/place lines; find the method that returns {'system':..., 'context':...} near cloudflare.py line 447) after the card is revealed AND carried by Kristin, and record exactly which lines the narrator is given about the card (is it shown as carried, in view, placed, hidden?) and whether the NPC speaker context mentions the card at all. (5) Conclude whether possession, observer knowledge and concealment are three separate, validated facts, or whether any of them is conflated (for example 'carried' standing in for 'concealed', or any NPC context treating a carried item as visible to the NPC). Remember what you cannot check offline: whether the live narrator describes the NPC seeing a pocketed card; say so in the Verdict.

TASK B: 1A WITHOUT THE DRAWER. Files: tests/test_drawer_avoidance_repro.py and /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/stage5-notes/drawer-avoidance-repro.md.
QUESTION (from .plans/implementation_plan.md Stage 5 item 4): 'Replay ... 1A avoiding the drawer ... cases.' What happens to a player who never opens or searches the drawer in scene 1A? Is the rest of the story still reachable and coherent, or does skipping the drawer strand later reveals or leave a wrong state?
KNOWN SO FAR (verify): in 1A the drawer search earns k_sl_1a_b_r0 (the memory card, sets memory_card_recovered); 'Open the drawer.' earns k_sl_1a_f_r1; k_sl_1a_b_r2 requires memory_card_recovered; scenes also leave by timer or forced handoff (data/stories/continuity-initiative/pacing.yaml, handoffs.yaml; see how storygame/runtime/engine.py forces handoffs and deliveries).
INVESTIGATE AND PIN: (1) Static dependency graph: parse data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml (via the loaded package, not by hand) and list every fact established ONLY by drawer-dependent reveals in 1A (k_sl_1a_b_r0, k_sl_1a_f_r1 and anything whose requires chain through memory_card_recovered or the drawer facts), then every reveal, storylet, handoff or route in LATER scenes whose requires depends (transitively) on those facts; give id and scene. (2) Dynamic replay: drive the real engine with a scripted provider through 1A using only commands that cannot match any drawer evidence (for example 'Look around.', 'Examine Michelle's phone.', 'Search the truck.', 'Walk around the building.') until the scene changes by timer/forced handoff, with a hard cap of 60 turns; report the turn count, the exit cause (transition_cause), which 1A reveals were earned, which authored deliveries the forced handoff injected, and the state of the memory_card and memory_card_recovered at the moment of leaving.
